errors.problem: Not fixed since round 2 (#4). In الْأَرْقَام الْعَرَبِيَّة ('Arabic numerals') and الْقَهْوَةُ الْعَرَبِيَّة ('Arabic coffee') the word is a feminine adjective agreeing with the noun before it, not the noun 'the Arabic language'. The coffee titleSegs correctly say 'Arabic · adj'. The tap teaches the learner to read 'the numbers, the Arabic language'.
errors.alsoChange: only in these two lines; where the word really is the language (science sentences, calligraphy sentences[0].sentences[1]) keep 'Arabic (the language)'

errors.problem: Not fixed since round 2 (#6). In يَسْكُنُ أَكْثَرُ الْبَدْوِ الْيَوْمَ فِي الْمُدُن ('most Bedouin live in cities') أَكْثَرُ + definite noun means 'most (of)'. The tap says only 'more', which contradicts the English of the same line and the sentence segs ('most (of)').

Not fixed since round 2 (#8). In لِأَنِّي اِبْنُهُ الْأَكْبَر the sense is 'his eldest son', and the English of the same line says 'eldest'. The tap gives 'the biggest'. The reading segs correctly say 'the eldest'.
Not fixed since round 2 (#9). هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا has no وَ; the gloss adds an 'and' that is not in the Arabic, so the learner may think مَرِيئًا contains wa-.
errors.alsoChange: the source seg in words[9].segs: ["مَرِيئًا", "and may it be wholesome"] → ["مَرِيئًا", "wholesome, may it be wholesome"]

errors.problem: The tap gloss lists 'more' twice (a merge glitch) and adds 'the most', which does not fit تَفَضَّلْ، كُلْ أَكْثَر ('please, eat more'). The sentence and reading segs correctly say 'more'.
errors.alsoChange: if the multi-sense gloss is kept elsewhere, at least remove the duplicate: 'more; the most (before a noun)'

errors.problem: These lines teach the meaning of the names ('أَمَل means hope and نُور means light'), but the tap shows only the first name, with no meaning. Round 3 says words that are both a name and a common word show both readings; كَرِيم in the same lines does (generous; Karim), أَمَل and نُور do not. (In quiz[3].prompt the name-only gloss is fine, because the meaning is the answer.)
errors.fix: أَمَل=hope; Amal (first name) · نُور=light; Nour (first name)
errors.alsoChange: only in sections[3].body[0] and quiz[3].explain (نُور); leave the reading segs (sister's/mother's name) as they are

After يَا a definite-by-address singular noun (munādā) is built on ḍamma: يَا أُسْتَاذُ. The word is in the middle of the phrase (the name follows), so it is not a pause form; the line teaches yā ustādh Sāmī with no vowel.

notes.note: اِسْمُهُ كَرِيم الْمِصْرِيّ: a first name followed by a surname normally keeps its tanwīn in full vocalisation (كَرِيمٌ الْمِصْرِيُّ). Not reported as an error because pause-style vocalisation of names is common in teaching material, but it is inconsistent with the course's full harakat elsewhere.
The English text spells the name 'Nur', while the tap gloss and the rest of the app say 'Nour'. Harmless, but one spelling would be cleaner.

اللّٰهُ أَكْرَم has a ḍamma on اللّٰهُ, but the ⟶ line reads 'llāh akram' / 'Allāh akram' (no -u), unlike every other nominative before a following word. Probably a deliberate treatment of the divine name; worth checking.

summary: I read the whole culture export (2,804 lines, 10 chapters: calligraphy, coffee, desert, family, food, places, ramadan, science, souq) and checked every Arabic line (558 Arabic strings with ⟶ lines, 234 segs lines) for harakat, case after kāna/inna/prepositions, idāfa, diptotes (مِصْرَ، دِمَشْقَ، مَسْقَطَ، صَحْرَاءَ، مَلَابِسَ، إِسْحَاقَ), verb-first agreement, non-human plural agreement, number–noun agreement, the mistake cards, translations and every quiz key; and all 876 tap glosses in 324 tap lines. The Arabic itself is clean: no wrong answer key, translation, rule or mistake card, and most round-2 fixes are in (بُرْجٍ، مَكَانٍ، كَرِيم, أَقْدَمُ, مِنْ, وَادِي, يَصُومُ, the ٢٨ digits). I found 10 errors, all minor: 1 Arabic string (يَا أُسْتَاذ without its ḍamma in mid-phrase), 7 tap glosses (about 9 tap entries wrong or misleading in their line: four round-2 glosses still unfixed — الْعَرَبِيَّة as 'the language', أَكْثَرُ 'more' for 'most', الْأَكْبَر 'the biggest' for 'the eldest', مَرِيئًا with an extra 'and' — plus two duplicated merged glosses and name-only glosses for أَمَل/نُور where the meaning is taught), and 2 engine patterns: clitics still written solid (bikhayr, biqalamin, Wabākistāna) despite the round-3 hyphen rule, and names lower-cased in some forms (bintu karīm, fī miṣr, ramaḍān, l-qāhirati).
